From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: Embeddings model fit validation - next steps

Hi Anna - great to meet earlier. Quick recap + concrete next steps from our discovery on semantic search/embeddings: 

Recap
- Goal: improve semantic search relevance for product FAQs and long-tail support queries (~250k docs).
- Current pain: sparse recall on paraphrases and drifting terms in last 6 months.

Our recommendations (initial):
1) Models to evaluate: redwood-emb-2.1 (128-d), open-embed-768 (768-d, baseline), and a quantized redwood-emb-2.1-qa variant for cost-sensitive routes.
2) Metrics: recall@10, NDCG@10, MRR, and pairwise A/B on annotated queries; cosine similarity distributions and minimum acceptable thresholds per intent.
3) Dimensionality checks: run 64/128/768 projections to measure tradeoffs between latency/cost and semantic separation (silhouette score).
4) Drift and freshness: time-bucketed evaluation (last 30/90/365 days) and a small drift detector on embedding distance to older corpus.

Deliverables we can run during POC:
- Benchmark harness that computes recall@k, NDCG, MRR over your annotated set (we can run on a 10k sample).
- Prompt sets / query templates for the FAQ + support clusters (please share a few hundred example queries).
- Config file for embeddings (batch size, quantization target, cache policy).

Attachments and links
- Attached: embeddings_bench_v1.csv (stub: sample eval pairs + labels).
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEmbeddingsBench (initial runbook + metrics dashboards).

Asks / next steps
- Can you share a ~1k sample of queries with ground-truth doc ids (even a small anonymized set is fine)?
- Are there any guardrails on dimensionality or latency we should respect (e.g., 50ms p50 on embed call)?
- Would you like us to run the initial benchmark and share a short deck by EoD Friday (Mar 25)?

I'll loop in Marissa and Rishi for the evaluation plan and schedule. Thanks again - looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Looping on this - quick internal note before we run: 
- Watch out for quality regressions vs their current baseline (they may be using an older in-house embedder). We should run a differential quality test with paired statistical significance (bootstrap CIs).
- Include long-tail bucket tests (tail defined as queries with term frequency < 5).
- Dimensionality: let's explicitly test 64/128/768 to show cost vs quality curve - include a t-SNE/UMAP snapshot in the deliverable to highlight clustering.
- Drift: compute mean embedding centroid distance per quarter and flag if mean increases by >10% relative to baseline.

I'll draft an eval_config.yml and send to Rishi for the runner. Keep Marcus in the loop for customer comms.

- Marissa
Sr. Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference
